label: SoundnessBench_general_c5_v1
original_text: We will intentionally introduce severe methodological flaws (e.g., mismatched datasets and metrics) into high-soundness proposals to test if models can detect these obvious errors.
modified_text: We will intentionally introduce severe methodological flaws (e.g., mismatched datasets and metrics) into proposals of varying soundness to test if models can detect these obvious errors.
explanation: The mechanism of this error is the introduction of a confounding variable. The original design uses "high-soundness" proposals as a clean baseline. By changing this to "proposals of varying soundness," the experiment is no longer a controlled test. If a model fails to detect the *injected* flaw, it could be because it was distracted by other, pre-existing (and undocumented) flaws in the base proposal. The experiment can no longer claim to be specifically testing the detection of the *intentionally-injected* flaws.
reasoning: The change introduces a confounding variable, making it impossible to isolate the effect of the intentionally introduced flaws, which is a classic experimental design flaw.
